verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II is scheduled for launch on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch ... on Wednesday, April 1'; R2: 'Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC'; R4: 'NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact launch date as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R2: 'Launch site Kennedy, LC-39B'; R4: 'launch from Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly confirm Kennedy Space Center as the launch site.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will send four astronauts on a 10-day trip around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The 10-day mission will send four astronauts on a journey around the moon'; R2: 'Crew size 4 ... crewed lunar flyby mission'; R4: 'The 10-day mission will send four astronauts on a journey around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly match four astronauts, 10-day mission (R2 specifies ~9-10 days), lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: Artemis II serves as a critical test flight for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'This flight is a crucial test for future crewed lunar landings'; R2: 'test flight supporting subsequent Artemis missions aimed at returning humans to the lunar surface'; R4: 'This flight is a crucial test for future crewed lunar landings'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm it as a test for future lunar landings.

verifications.claim: SpaceX is not directly responsible for the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's massive Space Launch System rocket ... SpaceX is planning a much more routine rocket launch for Thursday'; R2: 'Rocket Space Launch System'; R3: 'SLS ... Boeing, Lockheed Martin'; R4: 'NASA's massive Space Launch System spacecraft ... SpaceX is planning ... Thursday'
verifications.reasoning: Sources attribute Artemis II to NASA SLS/Orion (Boeing/Lockheed), SpaceX has separate launch.

verifications.claim: SpaceX is developing the Starship HLS (Human Landing System) for landing astronauts on the lunar surface during later missions.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference mentions 'Starship', 'HLS', or SpaceX developing a specific system for Artemis landings.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission will use NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Space Launch System rocket ... Orion spacecraft'; R2: 'second flight of the Space Launch System (SLS) and the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft'; R3: 'Space Launch System rocket ... Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft/capsule for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: SpaceX has a contract to provide the Human Landing System (HLS) for future later-phase Artemis lunar landings.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R5: 'SpaceX is one of the companies to which NASA awarded a multibillion-dollar contract to build a lunar lander for the Artemis moon missions'
verifications.reasoning: R5 mentions SpaceX contract for Artemis lunar lander (implies HLS), but not explicitly 'HLS'.

verifications.label: OMITTED
